description: Executable row-level fixture for the CRATEADR-002A governance-check-gates owner batch. It proves the selected missing-association batch is classified crate-by-crate without expanding CRATEADR-002 into a 377-crate implementation epic.
source_test: CRATEADR-002A local invariant check: parse this JSON, assert row/action counts, assert manifest and authority paths resolve, and assert each row has a minimum_gate_rule for its classification.

traceability.kanban_title: CRATEADR-002A: missing-crate owner-batch ADR/design-doc gate fixture
traceability.parent_title: CRATEADR-002: missing crate ADR/design-doc triage backlog
traceability.parent_body:
Sources: /tmp/oyatie-crate-adr-coverage.md; /tmp/oyatie-crate-adr-coverage-all.json
Lane: governance/crate-design-docs
Blast radius: docs/metadata triage only; no crate implementation changes
Atomic exit: 370 root workspace missing-association crates plus 7 cloud-kernel crates are grouped into owner batches with required ADR/design-doc action: cite existing ADR, author ADR, reorg target, or retire/defer
Notes: Derived from crate→ADR coverage audit; must obey PARALLEL-001 before repo edits.

selected_owner_batch.rationale: Gate/tooling crates should carry direct lifecycle/authority metadata rather than relying on corpus mentions; one crate is also reorg-sensitive.

gate_contract.status: fixture-contract; no crate implementation change in CRATEADR-002A
row_invariants: every row names an existing Cargo.toml manifest under the selected owner batch
required_action is exactly one of cite_existing_adr, author_adr, reorg_target, retire, defer, retire_defer
cite_existing_adr rows carry at least one resolving authority_ref and a non-empty minimum_gate_rule
reorg_target rows carry follow_up_required=true and a non-empty reorg_reason instead of unconditional ADR citation
the fixture itself cites CRATEADR-002 parent body plus the coverage and owner-batch source artifacts
